title: NMR crystallography reveals active-site protonation states of Toho-1 beta-lactamase in complex with avibactam.
authors: Williams, Christopher G; Wang, Songlin; Carta, Veronica; Langan, Patricia S; Thome, Alexander F; Ramos, Sebastian A; Holmes, Jacob B; Ghosh, Rittik K; Weiss, Kevin L; Beran, Gregory J O; Hartman, Joshua D; Coates, Leighton; Rienstra, Chad M; Mueller, Leonard J
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文结合固态NMR、X射线和机器学习势能加速的DFT计算，解析Toho-1 β-内酰胺酶与avibactam复合物的活性位点质子化状态，虽以蛋白质结构为核心且涉及计算化学，但主要聚焦实验表征与机理验证，而非结构预测/采样/生成等计算建模方法创新。
abstract: The determination of active-site protonation states is critical for a full mechanistic understanding of enzyme catalysis and inhibition. Here, we employ NMR crystallography-the integrated combination of solid-state NMR spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and first-principles computational chemistry-to determine the protonation states of the active site of Toho-1 beta-lactamase in complex with the non-beta-lactam inhibitor avibactam. We report two X-ray crystal structures of the Toho-1:avibactam complex, along with high-field solid-state NMR measurements that enable near-complete backbone and side-chain resonance assignments. To overcome the computational scaling limits that have traditionally hindered NMR crystallography in large systems, we use an accelerated workflow in which machine-learning interatomic potentials enable efficient geometry refinement prior to density functional theory chemical shift calculations. For Toho-1, quantitative analysis of the active-site chemical shifts and chemical shift tensors using this hybrid protocol reveals that the key active-site side chains retain their canonical charge states in the presence of avibactam, with Lys73 and Lys234 protonated and positively charged, and Glu166 deprotonated and poised to function as a general base. Contrary to recent proposals suggesting that avibactam inhibits by suppressing essential proton transfers through pK(a) perturbations, our data point to a more direct chemical origin arising from the intrinsic resistance of the Ser70-avibactam carbamoyl linkage to hydrolysis.
abstract_zh: 活性位点质子化状态的确定对于全面理解酶催化和抑制机制至关重要。在此，我们采用NMR晶体学——固态NMR波谱、X射线衍射和第一性原理计算化学的集成组合——来确定Toho-1 β-内酰胺酶与非β-内酰胺抑制剂阿维巴坦复合物中活性位点的质子化状态。我们报告了Toho-1:阿维巴坦复合物的两个X射线晶体结构，以及高场固态NMR测量，这些测量实现了近乎完整的骨架和侧链共振归属。为了克服传统上阻碍NMR晶体学在大系统中应用的计算规模限制，我们使用了一种加速工作流程，其中机器学习原子间势能在密度泛函理论化学位移计算之前实现高效的几何优化。对于Toho-1，使用这种混合协议对活性位点化学位移和化学位移张量进行定量分析揭示，关键活性位点侧链在阿维巴坦存在下保持其典型电荷状态，其中Lys73和Lys234质子化并带正电荷，Glu166去质子化并准备作为通用碱发挥作用。与最近提出的阿维巴坦通过pK(a)扰动抑制必需质子转移来发挥抑制作用的建议相反，我们的数据指向一个更直接的化学起源，源于Ser70-阿维巴坦氨基甲酰键对水解的内在抗性。
